name: Suriname

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Chamber of Commerce and Industry quotes the registration fee for a sole proprietorship.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company (NV or BV) is incorporated through a notary and costs more to set up than a sole proprietorship.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: Search the name at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry first.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KKF)
launchSteps.plain: Every business registers in the commercial register. A company is incorporated through a notary.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Tax Administration
launchSteps.plain: You get your tax number and register for VAT (BTW). File your returns even when you have no sales.

launchSteps.label: Check the licence your activity needs
launchSteps.plain: Some activities, such as food, transport or health, need a permit from the ministry that supervises them.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register your employees and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you withhold wage tax and pay the social premiums each month.

incomeTax.label: Income tax
incomeTax.allowanceNote: no tax on the first SRD 3,000 a year
incomeTax.bracketText: 0% up to SRD 3,000, 8% up to SRD 14,000, 18% up to SRD 24,000, 28% up to SRD 38,000, then 38%

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: Register with the Tax Administration when you start. The standard rate is 10%, with 5% on water, electricity and cooking gas, and 0% on exports.
vat.filingNote: You file your BTW return every month.

calendar.monthlyText: File and pay your BTW (VAT) return for the previous month.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your income tax return with the Tax Administration.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay wage tax and social premiums for the previous month.
calendar.vatText: File your BTW return every month, even when you have no sales.

notes: Suriname has a 10% VAT (BTW) since January 2023. Sole proprietors pay income tax on their profit at 8% to 38%, and companies pay 36%.
The Tax Administration publishes the exact income tax thresholds each year, because the Surinamese dollar loses value quickly.
